notes: The catalogue entry for arduino-mega lists no ports; pins are named as printed on the board in the image ('2'..'13', 'GND').
The Mega GND used is the one next to AREF (top of the digital header), as drawn in the circuit image.

Breadboard bank mapping: the image is drawn with rows j-f in the upper half and a-e in the lower half, so the upper half is catalogue bank 'b' (rows f-j) and the lower half is bank 't' (rows a-e). The upper power rail with the black '-' line is treated as 'tn'.

Column positions were estimated from the image: each LED anode shares a column with its resistor (cols 2,4,6,8,10,12,15,17,20,23,26,28) and the cathode sits in the next column (3,5,7,9,11,13,16,18,21,24,27,29).

Each resistor spans the centre gap (upper-half row f to lower-half row e); the signal wire from the Mega pin goes into the lower half in the resistor's column, so the pin connects through the resistor to the LED anode.

The short black jumpers run from the ground rail to each LED's cathode column (shown ending at row i); the rail hole used (tn.<n>) is arbitrary since the rail is one strip. One black wire (wire0) connects Mega GND to the rail.
Resistors are 220 ohm and LEDs red per the manual; the anode is the longer leg, drawn on the column that has the resistor.
